messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@unicorn.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Workload telemetry digest & SLO checkpoints

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying asks so we can finalize a throughput sizing recommendation for the PoC. TL;DR: we want the production SLOs you care about, plus a short traffic signature to size tokens/sec and concurrency.

Recap (what we captured)
- Primary feature: real-time summarization + agent-style followups (streaming enabled).
- Target model family: open-weights Llama-3 / similar (you mentioned model size flexible).
- Typical request: ~120 input tokens, median response ~85 tokens; some long responses up to 800 tokens.
- Traffic shape: steady-state 15–25 QPS, burst windows up to ~110 QPS for 90s.
- Concurrency observed in traces: steady ~18 concurrent inferences, peaks ~130 concurrent.
- Streaming: required for web UI; prefer chunked responses every ~250 tokens or ~200ms.

SLOs we discussed (please confirm or correct)
- p50 end-to-end response latency (streaming first-chunk): <= 80 ms
- p95 end-to-end (first chunk): <= 250 ms
- p99 tail: <= 600 ms (tolerable for non-interactive batch flows)
- Availability target: 99.9%

Requests for sizing (can you provide these items?)
1) A 24‑hour sample of request timestamps and response token counts (CSV or JSONL).
2) Percentile distribution of sequence lengths (input and output), ideally p50/p90/p99.
3) Typical client concurrency per region (do bursts come from a single region?).
4) Any streaming chunking behavior (e.g., flush every N tokens or time interval).

What we'll produce after we get the above:
- A short workload signature (tokens/sec, QPS, concurrency), and a recommended deployment profile (Hosted vs Dedicated) with approximate GPU-hour estimates.
- A concise SLO checklist and quick config for KV prefix caching and batching to hit p95 targets.

Attachments: I attached a tiny sample schema (workload_snapshot_sample.jsonl) and a template SLO checklist.

Next steps
- If you can drop the 24h sample and region info into the ticket or reply here by EOD Tuesday, Karthik and I will draft a 2-page sizing + config proposal.
- Proposed technical deep dive (30–45m): Tue Apr 6, 10:00 PT — if that works, Monica will send calendar invite.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and attaching a compact traffic export (unicorn_traffic_profile.csv) and a short note on streaming. Answers inline:

- 24h sample: attached CSV (timestamps, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, region).
- Sequence length percentiles (input/output): p50 110/80, p90 420/360, p99 760/820.
- Steady vs peak: steady 18 QPS (12–25), sustained peaks: multiple short bursts reaching 100–120 QPS for ~60–120s, roughly 3–4 times/day tied to product promotions.
- Concurrency: steady 14–20 active; instantaneous concurrency ceiling seen at 130 when multiple clients rejoin after a deployment.
- Streaming behavior: clients flush partial chunks on two triggers — token count (every 250 tokens) and time (if >200ms since last chunk). That means streaming-first-chunk latency matters a lot.

Additional notes:
- TLS termination is in us-west-2 for most traffic.
- We will need request-level logging retained for 30 days, and audit logs for 90 days.
- Security: SOC2 in progress; must provide IP allowlist for Dedicated options.

Attaching: unicorn_traffic_profile.csv

Happy to join the technical deep dive next Tue. Cheers,
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Workload telemetry digest & SLO checkpoints

Alex — appreciate the speedy export, very helpful. Quick preliminary sizing notes and a few clarifying technical asks before we finalize numbers: 

Preliminary sizing (ballpark) based on provided percentiles and streaming pattern:
- Tokens/sec steady: ~ (18 QPS * (110 input + 80 output)) ≈ 3,420 tokens/sec (steady)
- Burst tokens/sec: at 120 QPS -> ~ (120 * 190) ≈ 22,800 tokens/sec during peak windows
- Concurrency: plan for sustained concurrency headroom = 40 (2x steady) and burst headroom = 160 (to cover inflation + retry storms)

Model / runtime suggestions:
- For lowest-cost hosted path: Llama-3-7B quantized with aggressive batching for non-streamed responses; use streaming-optimized path for UI with smaller per-request batch windows.
- For tight p95 targets and heavy streaming: Dedicated pool with NVL codegen kernels or Triton-accelerated path; we can hit p95 ~200–300ms for first chunk with tuned KV cache.

Clarifying asks
1) Do bursts happen from single region or multi-region (you mentioned mostly us-west-2; any EU clients?)
2) Are retries client-driven? If so, what retry policy (exponential backoff, immediate) — affects headroom.
3) What fraction of requests need full 800-token responses vs short summaries? Even a 5–10% long-response tail materially affects tokens/sec.

I'll put together an initial capacity table (GPU-hours, suggested instance types, expected cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated) and share before the Tue deep-dive.

-Karthik
